prompt: A satellite moves at a constant speed in a circular orbit around the Earth. Explain why the gravitational force acting on the satellite does zero work on it.
answer: The gravitational force acts towards the centre of Earth, which is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity (or displacement) of the satellite (theta = 90 degrees). Since cos(90 degrees) = 0 (or there is no displacement in the direction of the force), the work done is zero.

mark_scheme.criterion: states that gravitational force is perpendicular to velocity / motion / displacement (at 90 degrees)
explains that cos(90 degrees) = 0 OR there is no component of force along the displacement / no displacement in the direction of the force

hints: Consider the direction of the gravitational force relative to the circular path.
What is the value of cos(theta) when theta = 90 degrees?
solution: The gravitational force acts radially towards the centre of the Earth. In a circular orbit, the instantaneous displacement (motion) is tangential, so the force is always perpendicular to the displacement (theta = 90 degrees). Because W = Fs cos(theta) and cos(90 degrees) = 0, no work is done on the satellite.
teacher_walkthrough: Common misconception: students think gravitational force must do work because it is large.
Point out that speed remains constant because no mechanical work is done to change kinetic energy.

provenance.abstract_pattern: conceptual explanation of zero work in perpendicular field
